Health | Congressman Daniel Goldman Skip to main content 245 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-7944 X How Can I Help? Health Health care is a human right and no person in America should have to choose between high-quality, affordable health care and putting food on the table. Congressman Goldman is working to bring down the cost of prescription drugs and tackle the runaway cost of physical and mental health care by taking on huge pharmaceutical corporations and by fighting to expand access to Medicare, Medicaid, and other government-funded health care options to every American. Congressman Goldman has introduced:  Michelle Alyssa Go Act to increase the number of federal Medicaid-eligible in-patient psychiatric beds for individuals who are seeking treatment for both mental health and substance use disorders Strengthening Medicaid for Serious Mental Illness Act to support individuals living with serious mental illnesses (SMI) such as schizophrenia, bipolar illness, and major depressive disorder Congressman Dan Goldman is a member of the Mental Health Caucus and the Bipartisan Health and Substance Use Disorder Task Force.    More on Health Image Goldman, Nadler Introduce New Legislation to Provide Previously Denied Compensation for 9/11 Families July 16, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. - U.S. Representatives Dan Goldman (NY-10) and Jerry Nadler (NY-12) introduced the No 9/11 Family Left Behind Act, legislation that would ensure that 9/11 victims’ families who were previously prevented from receiving financial compensation can finally get it. Specifically, the bill would amend the Justice for United States Victims of State Sponsored Terrorism (USVSST) Act to ensure that otherwise eligible 9/11 victims’ families who missed certain arbitrary deadlines and were therefore excluded from past distributions receive a lump-sum catch-up payment from the program. Housing | Congressman Daniel Goldman Skip to main content 245 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-7944 X How Can I Help? Housing New Yorkers deserve affordable, safe and reliable housing. Congressman Goldman is fighting for more and better housing, and to ensure that everyone can live with respect and dignity in their home. New York’s 10th Congressional District is home to over two dozen public housing developments as a part of the largest public housing authority in the country, NYCHA. Congressman Goldman is working tirelessly to ensure just and equitable treatment for public housing tenants and to get NYCHA the federal support it needs to serve hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers. The Congressman is also fighting to expand and preserve the Housing Choice Voucher Program, Section 8, while supporting those utilizing Section 8. Congressman Goldman has introduced:  Public Housing Emergency Response Act to allocate $70 billion in funding for public housing capital repairs and upgrades throughout the country – $32 billion of the allotted aid would be expected to flow directly to the New York City Housing Authority  Congressman Goldman is a member of the Renters Caucus. More on Housing Image Goldman Introduces New Legislation to Install AEDs in NYCHA Housing, Other Public Housing Projects June 5, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C. - U.S. Representative Dan Goldman (NY-10) introduced new legislation to help install Automated External Defibrillators, lifesaving devices that help immediately treat cardiac arrests by restoring a heartbeat, in federally-assisted multifamily residential buildings, including NYCHA. The Residential AED and CPR Preparedness Act of 2026 would authorize a $25 million annual grant program for five years to eligible entities to support access to AEDs and CPR. Funding could be used to support AED and CPR training for residents and building staff; purchase and maintain AEDs for use in multifamily buildings; and establish cardiac emergency response plans. This bill could support the placement of an estimated 75,000 AEDs in multifamily buildings. Issues : Congress Housing In the District Health Read More

Economy | Congressman Daniel Goldman Skip to main content 245 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-7944 X How Can I Help? Economy Access to the American Dream is a promise that must be available to every single person in our nation. Congressman Goldman is committed to fulfilling this promise by raising wages, protecting and expanding the right to unionize in the workplace, and making sure our economy delivers for working families, not just the wealthy and well-connected. To increase opportunity for all, families must also have access to universal child care, affordable health care, affordable housing, and paid family leave. Congressman Goldman is fighting for progressive tax policies to ensure that corporations and the wealthy pay their fair share so that we can make these critical investments. Congressman Goldman is a member of the Labor Caucus.    More on Economy Goldman Introduces New Legislation To Protect Users Of Buy Now, Pay Later June 17, 2026 Press Release U.S. Representative Dan Goldman (NY-10) introduced new legislation to protect users of Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL). These practices harm consumers by making it virtually impossible to comparison shop and by hindering competitive markets. Education | Congressman Daniel Goldman Skip to main content 245 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-7944 X How Can I Help? Education A high-quality public education should be guaranteed to all children and families in America, regardless of their zip code. Studies have found that early childhood education has long-lasting advantages beyond academic performance. Congressman Goldman is fighting for more investment in our schools and teachers, to increase federal funding for pre-K programs, and to expand childcare and early childhood education opportunities. Congressman Dan Goldman is also fighting to ensure that higher education is more accessible to all Americans. He is pushing to codify the SAVE Plan and introduce tax credits to student loan borrow to reduce the impacts of student loan debt. Congressman Goldman has introduced:  GRADUATE Act to enact a long overdue expansion of the Student Loan Interest Deduction for the first time since 2001, raising the deduction to $10,000 for qualifying borrowers and covering payments of the student loan principal for the first time Codifying SAVE Plan Act to enshrine the Biden Administration’s historic student loan repayment plan into federal law, protecting the critical regulation from rollbacks by future presidential administrations    More on Education Image Goldman Introduces New Legislation to Invest $10 Billion Annually in Afterschool Learning Programs May 7, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C. - Today, U.S. Representatives Dan Goldman (NY-10) and Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), founding members of the Congressional Dads Caucus, introduced the Afterschool for All Act, new legislation that would provide $10 billion in federal funding annually for 10 years after school and summer learning programming. The programming would be fully paid for by a 1% increase in the corporate income tax rate. Immigration | Congressman Daniel Goldman Skip to main content 245 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-7944 X How Can I Help? Immigration New York and our nation were built by immigrants, and anyone who wishes to come to this country in pursuit of the American Dream should be welcomed with open arms. Congressman Goldman is committed to advancing comprehensive immigration reform with a path to citizenship to promote family unity, protect Dreamers and TPS recipients, and create a more humane immigration system. By working to expand the lawful immigration process, streamline our immigration system, and clear the unconscionably large backlog of asylum claims, Congressman Goldman is working to make the immigration process easier for new arrivals. Congressman Goldman has introduced:  Children’s Court Act to combat the immigration court backlog and strengthen due process rights for children  More on Immigration Image Goldman, Cortez Masto, Crow, Padilla Slam Trump Administration’s Nonpayment for Legal Services for Unaccompanied Minors May 29, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C. - U.S. Representatives Dan Goldman (D-NY) and Jason Crow (D-CO) and U.S. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) and Alex Padilla (D-CA) are leading 70 lawmakers in demanding that the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) reimburse providers for work performed under their contract to furnish legal services to unaccompanied children. ORR has not issued reimbursements for services rendered since December 2025, despite Congress having appropriated funds for this purpose. The agency’s ongoing refusal to issue payments contravenes the Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act (TVPRA) requirements, appropriations directives, and the federal government’s contractual obligations.
